findings.asked: Factorise the numerator and denominator of an algebraic fraction and simplify.
findings.wentWrong: About a third got full marks. Most took the common factor 2 out (some just divided by 2 instead), then partial credit for a difference of two squares. Weaker candidates cancelled single terms across the fraction or tried to solve it as an equation.
findings.rule: Only common factors cancel; an expression is simplified, never solved.

findings.asked: Factorise (grouping in the numerator, difference of two squares in the denominator) and cancel.
findings.wentWrong: Most got a mark for taking 3 out of the denominator. The difference of two squares went wrong when the letter was not the first term, because candidates swapped the terms round; grouping in the numerator troubled the less able.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Kept the terms in their given order, wrote a squared minus b squared as (a + b)(a - b), and cancelled whole brackets.
findings.rule: 25 - w squared factorises as (5 + w)(5 - w) - do not reorder.

findings.asked: Divide one algebraic fraction by another and simplify.
findings.wentWrong: Only one in twenty finished. Most earned a mark or two for inverting the second fraction and factorising the denominators, then stalled.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Inverted, factorised every numerator and denominator, cancelled the common brackets, and wrote the single remaining fraction.
findings.rule: Flip, factorise everything, cancel whole brackets.

ruleToRemember: Factorise every numerator and denominator first (HCF, difference of two squares, grouping), invert the second fraction when dividing, and cancel only whole matching brackets.
aStarSignal: A division that needs three different factorising techniques before anything cancels, finished as one fraction in lowest terms.
